I am 68 years old, finished primary school. I have farmed these 14 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. My husband is 71 and we do the work ourselves. Our son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money home, but this land is still how we eat and live.

I plant wheat in winter and corn in summer on all 14 mu. I don't read books and I don't trust county officials who come in clean shoes telling me what to do. I learned from my father and I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang's wheat looks heavy and full, I ask him what he used and I copy him.

For the wheat: Last October I sowed improved seed, 30 jin per mu. I bought it from the seed dealer in town — the same kind Old Wang used, his wheat stood up well to the wind. Before sowing I ploughed the land deep. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's 100 jin, 50 kilograms. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I topdress 50 jin of urea per mu. I know some people say that's a lot, but I saw what happened two years ago when my neighbor Li used less — his wheat turned yellow and the heads were small. He lost 100 jin per mu. I would rather waste one bag of fertilizer than lose half my harvest. Fertilizer is money, but an empty grain bin is a disaster. I irrigate three times from my well: March for green-up, April at jointing, and May when the grain fills. Pumping costs electricity, but three times is enough if you do it right. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and spray for aphids and rust twice — once in April and once in May if the weather turns damp.

For the corn: Right after we cut the wheat in early June, I sow hybrid corn seed directly without ploughing. Everyone around here switched to no-tillage for corn. It saves diesel and time, and we have to get the seed in fast before the soil dries hard. I use 4 jin of seed per mu. At sowing I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. When the corn reaches the big trumpet stage, I spread 50 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the weather is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray herbicide once right after sowing, and insecticide once in July when the corn borers and armyworms come. Last year the worms were bad in the next village, so I watch carefully.

Last year my wheat yielded 1000 jin per mu and my corn yielded 1200 jin per mu. This year I expect the same — about 500 kg for wheat and 600 kg for corn. The dealer tried to sell me a new corn seed for 80 yuan more per mu. I said no. I have farmed long enough to know that fancy seed is a gamble, but urea and compound fertilizer never lie.
